# Email length validation on `POST /users`, status filter on `POST /reports/orders`

Two independent changes, each with its own tests. Branch
`alchemy/r1-email-and-report-status`, 6 commits on top of `d3b2f0a` (one per
change, two integration merges, two test-hardening commits), head `1205c14`.
Not pushed; no pull request opened.

| | |
|:--|:--|
| Base | `d3b2f0a` — 20 tests passing |
| Head | `1205c14` — 31 tests passing |
| Diff | 6 files, 192 insertions, 5 deletions |

## What changed

**(1) `POST /users` rejects an over-long email** — `src/users/service.js`

A `MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH = 254` constant and one check in `register`, which throws
`invalid(...)` and so returns 400, matching how every other rule in this
service reports bad input. The limit is measured on the **normalized** email —
after `normalizeEmail` trims and lowercases — because that is the value the
store persists and compares.

No code was added for the "exactly one `@` with a non-empty part on each side"
half of the requirement, because the existing `EMAIL_PATTERN`
(`/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`, unchanged since before this branch) already
rejects every such address: neither side may contain an `@`, and both must be
non-empty. A second parallel check would have been redundant validation on day
one. That half is now pinned by regression tests instead — see the caveat on
this in *Open items* below.

**(2) `POST /reports/orders` accepts an optional `status`** —
`src/orders/service.js`, `src/reports/routes.js`, `README.md`

`orders.all(status)` now validates and filters: an absent status exports every
order exactly as before, and any other value throws `invalid(...)` → 400. The
accepted set is `STATUSES = Object.keys(TRANSITIONS)`, derived from the
lifecycle table that already defined those five states, so the filter cannot
drift out of sync with the lifecycle and the reports subsystem never holds a
status list of its own.

The reports handler computes its rows **before** `fs.mkdir` and `fs.writeFile`,
so a rejected status has no filesystem effect at all — no stray export file and
no created directory. `guard.requireAdmin` and the `{ name }` response shape are
untouched; a customer sending any status still gets 403, not 400.

Rejected, with reasons: filtering inside the reports route (would have put a
second copy of the status vocabulary in a subsystem that does not own it);
extracting pure validator modules (a structure this codebase uses nowhere
else, for one rung of earlier detection — see *Not verified*).

## Evidence

Every command below ran at the integrated head `1205c14`, and every result was
re-produced by an agent that wrote neither change. Commands, not summaries:

| Command | Exit | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `node --test` | 0 | tests 31, pass 31, fail 0 |
| `node --test test/users.test.js` | 0 | tests 9, pass 9, fail 0 |
| `node --test test/reports.test.js` | 0 | tests 11, pass 11, fail 0 |
| `node --test test/orders.test.js` | 0 | tests 6, pass 6, fail 0 |
| `node --test test/payments.test.js` | 0 | tests 4, pass 4, fail 0 |
| `node --test` at `d3b2f0a` | 0 | tests 20, pass 20, fail 0 — the baseline, re-measured rather than assumed |
| `git diff d3b2f0a 1205c14 --name-status` | 0 | six modified files, none added or deleted |
| `git diff -U0 d3b2f0a 1205c14 -- test/` | 0 | three hunks, all pure insertions: **zero** lines removed or modified under `test/` |

All 20 baseline tests still pass by name (the base name set is a subset of the
head's), and the pre-existing `admins export orders and download the export`
test is byte-identical to its `d3b2f0a` form.

### Tests added (11)

`test/users.test.js` — an email of exactly 254 normalized characters registers
(sent as 258 raw characters, padded and uppercased, so it also pins the
normalization basis); an email of 255 normalized characters is rejected;
registration rejects an email without exactly one `@` and a non-empty part on
each side (five cases: no `@`, two `@`, two `@` around a label, empty local
part, empty domain).

`test/reports.test.js` — one inclusion test per status value for `pending`/`paid`
(one test), `shipped`, `delivered` and `cancelled`, each asserting 201, the
matching order's row **present** and an adjacent-lifecycle-state order's row
**absent**, by order id rather than by row count; a header-only export for a
status no order is in; an unfiltered export across several states; six rejected
value shapes (unknown string, wrong case, empty string, `null`, a number, an
array) each 400 with the report directory listing unchanged; and a rejected
status not even creating the report directory. Both filterable states are
reached through the real HTTP API (pay then ship then deliver; cancel), not by
writing into the store.

### The assertions are not hollow

Thirteen mutants were run against the new tests, each in a throwaway copy of the
repository (never in the working tree), and all thirteen were killed:

- Five "silently drop status V" mutants and five "narrow the accepted enum by
  V" mutants, one per status value — **no survivor**, so every one of REQ-2's
  five values is pinned for both inclusion and acceptance.
- `src/users/service.js` reverted to `d3b2f0a`; the cap as `>=` instead of `>`;
  the cap applied to the raw instead of the normalized email — each killed by
  exactly one expected test.

This matters because it is what the first two review passes did *not* establish:
two mutants survived earlier revisions of this branch (`shipped`/`cancelled`,
then `delivered` had no inclusion coverage), and both were fixed by adding
tests, with no production change.

## Open items — known, deliberate, not fixed here

| | |
|:--|:--|
| `EMAIL_PATTERN` is stricter than the requirement | It also requires a dot in the domain, so `a@b` returns 400 — an address with exactly one `@`, non-empty sides and under 254 characters. This predates the branch and is unchanged by it. Requirement (1) is read as a **rejection rule** — it fixes what must be rejected, not what must be accepted — so the stricter pattern satisfies it. If the intent was the complete acceptance rule instead, say so and it becomes a separate change. |
| `254` is measured after normalization | A 258-character raw value that trims and lowercases to 254 is accepted. The requirement does not say which value is measured; `test/users.test.js` now pins the normalized reading deliberately, so reversing it is a test change as well as a code change. |
| The status list is hand-copied twice | `README.md` and the expected error string in `test/reports.test.js` each restate the five values that `TRANSITIONS` derives. Adding a sixth lifecycle state would fail as a string mismatch rather than a behaviour failure. No check keeps the copies in sync. |
| 403-before-400 has no test | A customer sending an invalid status gets 403 (authorization runs first), confirmed by hand but asserted by no test. |
| `node --test` counts `test/helpers.js` | It is discovered as a zero-test passing file, so the raw counts above overstate behavioural tests by one (19+1 at base, 30+1 at head). Pre-existing; every count quoted here is faithful to node's own output. |

## Not verified

- **No lint, type check, or CI.** This repository has no `eslint` config, no
  `tsconfig.json`, and no `.github/`; `package.json` defines only `test`. So
  `node --test` is the earliest capable gate that exists, and nothing ran at a
  stage before it. Validation logic errors are catchable one rung earlier
  (Stage 6, a pure predicate plus a unit test) than where they are caught here
  (Stage 7, in-process HTTP); that rung was left open deliberately, since
  extracting predicate modules introduces a structure the codebase uses nowhere
  else for one rung of earlier detection. Closing either gap is a separate
  increment.
- **Not run:** concurrent exports against one report directory; export-name
  collision inside the same millisecond; a `reportDir` the process cannot write;
  the 1 MiB body-limit path on this endpoint; exports spanning more than one
  page; non-BMP or IDN emails (JS `.length` counts UTF-16 code units, and the
  requirement says "characters").
- **Not measured:** suite wall-clock as a baseline for later optimization
  (`node --test` duration went 833 ms → 1332 ms as the suite grew from 20 to 31
  tests; no optimization pass ran, by design — that belongs to the iteration
  after this one ships).
- **Nothing was pushed**, no pull request was opened, and no commit used
  `--no-verify`.
